canvas-01.description: The map in the lower left of Sheet 1 of the December 1922 Beach Haven atlas, drawn at 100 feet to an inch inside a heavy frame, below the key map, the water facilities and fire department notes and the street index that fill the rest of the page. It covers the bay side of the old town centre between Little Egg Harbor Bay and Delaware Avenue, from Amber Street east to 2nd Street. West Avenue curves along the shore at the top, past the end of a slip and a long wharf; Pennsylvania Avenue crosses the middle; Delaware Avenue runs along the bottom. The cross streets are Amber, South, Center (drawn about 100 feet wide), Dock and 2nd Street. Most of the area is laid out in long narrow numbered lots (blocks 50 to 64) with almost no buildings: a few dwellings and auxiliary buildings on the block between Center and Dock streets south of Pennsylvania Avenue and two dwellings on Delaware Avenue. The built-up part is the waterfront east of Center Street, where a row of club houses, a hotel and wharves stands along the shore of a basin facing a large dock that projects into the bay. Water pipes (6 inch on West Avenue and Center Street) and hydrants are marked. The areas beyond Amber Street and beyond 2nd Street are lettered vacant. A compass rose and a scale bar are drawn on the map; north points to the upper right, as on every sheet of the atlas.
notes: South Street is now Engleside Avenue; Center Street is now Centre Street; Dock Street is now Dock Road.
Pennsylvania, Delaware and West Avenues are now North and South Pennsylvania Avenue, North and South Delaware Avenue and West Avenue / North West Avenue, divided at Centre Street.
Only this map is georeferenced; the key map of the whole town at the top of the sheet is not to scale for this purpose and is outside the mask.

Sheet 1 (100 ft): key map, index, water facilities and a 100 ft map in the lower left (Pennsylvania, Amber, South, Center, Dock, 2nd St, West Av, Delaware Av; yacht club docks). Only the lower-left map is configured; key map at top is outside the mask.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the bay side of the southern part of Beach Haven, between West Avenue at the top and Beach Avenue at the foot, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Four cross streets, Norwood Avenue, Berkeley Avenue, Ocean and Marine, run down the page between three wide avenues. West Avenue, labelled 100 feet wide, crosses the top and bends toward the right edge beyond Ocean; Bay Avenue, also about 100 feet wide, crosses the middle; Beach Avenue runs along the bottom edge. The upper blocks, numbered 82 to 84, are laid out in narrow lots and are almost entirely vacant, with a small dwelling on Norwood Avenue and the Beach Haven Yacht Club building at the top edge between Berkeley Avenue and Ocean. The lower blocks, numbered 123 to 125, between Bay and Beach avenues are better built up, with a scatter of frame dwellings, some with outbuildings, concentrated near Norwood Avenue and Berkeley Avenue, and a larger row of buildings along the Beach Avenue frontage. Lot numbers and frontage dimensions are lettered along the block lines, a four-inch water pipe is drawn down Ocean Street, and dash-line fire hydrant connections end at dots marked D.H. The sheet carries a compass rose, the Beach Haven date stamp of December 1922 and a scale of feet at the foot. Adjoining sheet numbers 3, 6 and 11 are printed in the margins.
notes: West Avenue, Bay Avenue and Beach Avenue are now South West Avenue, South Bay Avenue and South Beach Avenue; Norwood Avenue, Berkeley Avenue, Ocean Street and Marine Street keep their names.
Beach Haven Yacht Club building at the top edge between Berkeley Avenue and Ocean.
50 ft. West Av, Bay Av, Beach Av; Norwood, Berkeley, Ocean, Marine.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the blocks of the old town centre between Delaware Avenue at the top and Beach Avenue at the bottom, from Marine Street on the left to Amber Street on the right, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. Bay Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet. The cross streets are Marine, Pearl, Coral and Amber. The three blocks between Delaware and Bay Avenues (85, 86 and 87) are almost empty: the largest building is a brick garage on Bay Avenue between Pearl and Coral, and on the corner of Bay Avenue and Amber Street stands a row of brick stores and dwellings with a bank at the Coral Street corner and a long frame storage building behind them. The blocks between Bay and Beach Avenues (126, 127 and 128) are thinly built with frame dwellings and auxiliary buildings, most of them between Pearl and Amber streets. The Corinthian Yacht Club house stands at the corner of Marine Street and Beach Avenue. Water pipes, mostly 4 and 8 inch, run in Bay and Beach Avenues and the cross streets, with hydrants at the corners. House numbers are given in pairs on many frontages. Adjoining sheet numbers (2, 4, 7) are printed in the margins, and the scale bar sits in the lower right corner.
notes: Delaware, Bay and Beach Avenues south of Centre Street are now South Delaware Avenue, South Bay Avenue and South Beach Avenue.
Corinthian Yacht Club house at Marine Street and Beach Avenue; bank at Bay Avenue and Coral Street.
50 ft. Delaware, Bay, Beach Avs; Marine, Pearl, Coral, Amber. Pilot.

sheet-4-1.description: The main part of Sheet 4, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper right, covering the business centre of Beach Haven between Delaware Avenue at the top and the line of a correction slip pasted about halfway between Bay and Beach Avenues, from Amber Street (whose west side is drawn on Sheet 3) to Center Street. South Street and Center Street are drawn about 100 feet wide. Between Delaware and Bay Avenues the block from Amber to South Street holds the borough's pumping station and fire department: a fire house, gas engine pumping station, storage cisterns of 55,000 and 17,000 gallons, an elevated water tank of 100,000 gallons, a gasometer, a generator house and an acetylene gas machine. The block from South to Center Street holds the Beach Haven Ice and Cold Storage Company with its fish storage, and the Beach Haven Lumber Company's lumber sheds and stores, served by a railroad siding that crosses the block from the right. Beyond Center Street are the New Colonial motion picture theatre and, south of Bay Avenue, the Beach Haven House hotel. Frame dwellings, stores and small shops line Bay Avenue south of the street. The upper left of the sheet is a separate strip drawn on its own (part 2) and the lower part is the correction slip (part 3).
notes: South Street is now Engleside Avenue and Center Street is Centre Street; both are drawn about 100 feet wide.
The lower part of the sheet is a pasted correction slip drawn about one block (some 260 ft) to the left of this part's alignment; it is georeferenced separately as part 3.
Beach Haven Ice and Cold Storage Co., Beach Haven Lumber Co., fire department and pumping station, New Colonial motion pictures, Beach Haven House.

50 ft. Three parts: 1 main map (Delaware Av to the slip line south of Bay Av, Amber to Center St); 2 strip at upper left behind a paper join (Dock St and 2nd St, Delaware Av to south of Bay Av; continues the main map east of Center St); 3 correction slip pasted across the lower part (Beach Av frontage, Amber to 2nd St), drawn about one block left of part 1's alignment.

sheet-4-2.description: A narrow strip at the upper left of Sheet 4, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and set apart from the main map by a paper join, showing the block between Dock Street and 2nd Street from Delaware Avenue to Bay Avenue (block 91) and the corner of the block south of Bay Avenue beyond. It continues the main part of the sheet eastward, past Center Street, and is placed on the left only to fit the page. Dock Street is drawn 40 feet wide and 2nd Street 60 feet north of Bay Avenue and 80 feet south of it, where the street is drawn shifted. A railroad siding crosses the strip just below Delaware Avenue. The block between Dock and 2nd streets is divided into lots with only two dwellings near Bay Avenue; south of Bay Avenue stand a few dwellings and a long shed facing Bay Avenue. Water pipes (4 inch) run along 2nd Street and a hydrant stands at the Bay Avenue corner. The sheet title cartouche (Beach Haven, N.J., Dec. 1922) and the sheet number are printed at the top of the strip.
notes: Dock Street is now Dock Road.
2nd Street is drawn about 30 ft further left south of Bay Avenue than north of it; the modern street is straight.
Placed from two detected junctions on Delaware Avenue and a hand-picked point at Dock and Bay; low confidence.

50 ft. Three parts: 1 main map (Delaware Av to the slip line south of Bay Av, Amber to Center St); 2 strip at upper left behind a paper join (Dock St and 2nd St, Delaware Av to south of Bay Av; continues the main map east of Center St); 3 correction slip pasted across the lower part (Beach Av frontage, Amber to 2nd St), drawn about one block left of part 1's alignment.

sheet-4-3.description: A correction slip pasted across the lower part of Sheet 4, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. It shows the southern halves of blocks 129, 130 and 131 between Bay and Beach Avenues and the frontage of Beach Avenue from Amber Street to 2nd Street, and is drawn about one block to the left of the main part of the sheet, so it is georeferenced on its own. Center Street is drawn 100 feet wide. The blocks are closely built with frame dwellings, stores and auxiliary buildings: a garage and stores between Amber and South streets, the post office and stores on Beach Avenue between South and Center streets, and between Center and 2nd streets the Ocean House and The Magnolia, two boarding houses or small hotels. House numbers on Beach Avenue run from 701 to 714, with older numbers beside many of them. Water pipes of 4 and 8 inches run in the streets, with hydrants at the Beach Avenue corners. Below Beach Avenue the slip shows the tops of the blocks drawn on Sheet 8 and the scale bar.
notes: The slip is drawn about one block (some 260 ft) to the left of the main part of the sheet; placed by a helmert fit on four junctions along Beach Avenue (Amber, South, Center, 2nd).
South Street is now Engleside Avenue; Center Street is Centre Street.
Post office, Ocean House and The Magnolia on this part.

50 ft. Three parts: 1 main map (Delaware Av to the slip line south of Bay Av, Amber to Center St); 2 strip at upper left behind a paper join (Dock St and 2nd St, Delaware Av to south of Bay Av; continues the main map east of Center St); 3 correction slip pasted across the lower part (Beach Av frontage, Amber to 2nd St), drawn about one block left of part 1's alignment.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the bay side of the central part of Beach Haven, between Delaware Avenue at the top and Beach Avenue at the foot, and from 2nd Street on the left to 5th Street on the right, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Across the upper third of the sheet runs the Long Beach Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad), a pair of tracks with sidings, with the Beach Haven railroad station and its ticket office standing on the line between 3rd and 4th streets. Railroad Avenue, 80 feet wide, lies along the south side of the tracks, and the blocks between it and Bay Avenue, numbered 92, 94 and 95, hold the station area, a repairing and tin shop and a few small outbuildings. Bay Avenue, 100 feet wide, crosses the middle of the sheet. Below it the blocks numbered 132, 133 and 134 extend to Beach Avenue and are built up with frame dwellings, outbuildings and, on the 3rd to 4th street block, a colonial motion picture theatre. Beach Avenue at the foot is drawn only 33 feet wide, and an eight-inch water pipe runs along it, with four-inch pipes down the cross streets and fire hydrant connections marked D.H. Second Street shifts to the left where it crosses Bay Avenue. The sheet carries a compass rose and the Beach Haven date stamp at the top, and the margins give the numbers of adjoining sheets 4, 9 and 12.
notes: Bay Avenue is now North Bay Avenue; Delaware Avenue is now North Delaware Avenue, whose modern line may follow part of the railroad; Railroad Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap today.
The Long Beach Railroad has been removed; no rail control was used.
Beach Haven railroad station between 3rd and 4th streets.
50 ft. Delaware, Railroad Av, Bay, Beach; 2nd to 5th St; railroad (P.R.R. depot).

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the ocean side of the southern part of Beach Haven, from Beach Avenue at the top, across Atlantic Avenue, to the shoreline and the Atlantic Ocean, and from Norwood Avenue on the left to Marine on the right. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Beach Avenue, 60 feet wide, runs along the top with an eight-inch water pipe, and Atlantic Avenue, 50 feet wide, crosses below the middle. The cross streets are Norwood Avenue, Berkeley Avenue, Ocean and Marine. Between Beach and Atlantic avenues the blocks numbered 161 to 163 hold a scattering of frame dwellings and outbuildings, some of them large, and one building near the top between Berkeley Avenue and Ocean is coloured as a different construction. Below Atlantic Avenue the blocks numbered 199 to 201 are laid out in lots but are entirely vacant. A boardwalk, lettered in spaced letters and carrying short yellow piers or groynes at intervals, follows the line of the shore, below which the beach, the surf line and the open ocean take up the bottom third of the sheet. Four-inch water pipes run down the cross streets and fire hydrant connections end at dots marked D.H. The sheet carries a compass rose and the Beach Haven date stamp of December 1922 at the top, and the margins name adjoining sheets 2, 7 and 11.
notes: Beach Avenue and Atlantic Avenue are now South Beach Avenue and South Atlantic Avenue; Norwood Avenue, Berkeley Avenue, Ocean Street and Marine Street keep their names.
The fitted scale (about 8.3 px per foot) is about 3 percent above the 8.0 of the other 50 foot sheets; the street spacing on the sheet is that much wider than the modern street grid.
The boardwalk lettering is spaced and only partly legible.
50 ft. Beach, Atlantic Avs to the ocean; Norwood, Berkeley, Ocean, Marine.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the ocean side of the middle of Beach Haven, from Beach Avenue at the top, across Atlantic Avenue, to the shore and the Atlantic Ocean, and from Marine at the left to Amber at the right. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. The block numbered 164, between Marine and Pearl, is filled by the Hotel Baldwin, a large irregular frame hotel with a kitchen, dining room, laundry, ice house and help's quarters, with a note on the water supply and watchman below it. Blocks 165 and 166, between Pearl and Coral and between Coral and Amber, hold a loose scatter of detached frame dwellings with outbuildings, laid out on narrow lots, with a few vacant parcels near Pearl. Beach Avenue, 33 feet wide with an eight-inch water pipe, runs along the top, and Atlantic Avenue, 50 feet wide, crosses below the blocks. South of it the ocean-front blocks numbered 202 to 204 are mostly empty, apart from the Hotel Baldwin bath houses and a shed on the left and a small building near Coral. A boardwalk with yellow piers follows the shore below the blocks, beyond which the beach, the surf line and the ocean fill the lower part of the sheet. The cross streets carry four-inch water pipes, and fire hydrant connections end at dots marked D.H. A compass rose and the Beach Haven date stamp of December 1922 are drawn at the left and right of the top margin.
notes: Beach Avenue and Atlantic Avenue are now South Beach Avenue and South Atlantic Avenue; Marine, Pearl, Coral and Amber are now Marine Street, Pearl Street, Coral Street and Amber Street.
Hotel Baldwin occupies block 164 between Marine and Pearl.
50 ft. Beach, Atlantic Avs to the ocean; Marine, Pearl, Coral, Amber; Hotel Baldwin.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the ocean side of the central part of Beach Haven, from Beach Avenue at the top, across Atlantic Avenue, to the shore and the Atlantic Ocean, and from Amber at the left to 2nd Street at the right. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. The long block numbered 167 on the left holds the Engleside Hotel, a large frame building with a long ballroom and parlors wing, kitchen, laundry and help's quarters, with a note that it is closed in winter and watched by a watchman; a separate cottage stands to its left. Block 168, between South and Center, holds the Episcopal church, a few dwellings and a store. Block 169, between Center and 2nd Street, holds the Kynett M.E. Church, heated by furnace and lit by electricity, the public library and a scatter of detached frame dwellings. Center is drawn 100 feet wide with a four-inch water pipe, while Beach Avenue is 33 feet wide with an eight-inch pipe and Atlantic Avenue is 50 feet wide. South of Atlantic Avenue the ocean-front blocks numbered 205 to 207 are vacant except for the Engleside Hotel bath houses and a platform on the left. A boardwalk with yellow piers follows the shore, with the beach, surf line and ocean below. The sheet carries a compass rose and the Beach Haven date stamp of December 1922, and the margins name adjoining sheets 4, 7 and 9.
notes: Beach Avenue and Atlantic Avenue are now South Beach Avenue and South Atlantic Avenue (North Atlantic Avenue and Beach Avenue east of Centre Street); South is now Engleside Avenue; Center is now Centre Street; Amber is now Amber Street.
Kynett M.E. Church, the public library and the Engleside Hotel are named on the sheet.
50 ft. Beach, Atlantic Avs to the ocean; Amber, South, Center, 2nd St; Engleside Hotel.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the ocean side of the north central part of Beach Haven, from Beach Avenue at the top, across Atlantic Avenue, to the shore and the Atlantic Ocean, and from 2nd Street on the left to 5th Street on the right. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Beach Avenue is drawn 33 feet wide with an eight-inch water pipe, Atlantic Avenue 50 feet, and the cross streets 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th streets are 80 feet with four-inch pipes. Between Beach and Atlantic avenues, block 170 on the left holds a few dwellings and outbuildings, and block 171, between 3rd and 4th streets, holds St. Thomas Aquinas Catholic Church, heated by furnace and lit by oil or electricity, together with a close scatter of small frame dwellings on narrow lots. Block 172, between 4th and 5th streets, is laid out in lots but vacant. South of Atlantic Avenue the ocean-front blocks numbered 208 to 210 are vacant apart from one small building on block 208. A boardwalk, lettered along its length, runs with yellow piers along the shore, with the beach, the surf line and the open ocean below. Fire hydrant connections end at dots marked D.H. The sheet carries a compass rose and the Beach Haven date stamp of December 1922, and the margins name adjoining sheets 5, 8 and 12.
notes: Beach Avenue keeps its name and Atlantic Avenue is now North Atlantic Avenue; 2nd to 5th streets are 2nd Street to 5th Street.
St. Thomas Aquinas Catholic Church stands on block 171.
50 ft. Beach, Atlantic Avs to the ocean; 2nd to 5th St.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the southern end of the Beach Haven peninsula at 100 feet to an inch, from Pennsylvania Avenue near the top edge to the Atlantic Ocean at the foot, and from Nelson Avenue at the left to Iroquois Avenue at the right, with north toward the upper right. The sheet is a plat of numbered blocks and lots rather than a built-up district: West Avenue, Bay Avenue, Beach Avenue and Atlantic Avenue cross it as wide streets, West Avenue drawn 100 feet and Bay Avenue 94 feet wide, with eight-inch water pipes, and eight narrow cross streets run down the page. Blocks 30 to 36 across the top, 66 to 72 below West Avenue, 107 to 114 on either side of Bay Avenue, 145 to 152 between Beach and Atlantic avenues and 183 to 190 along the ocean front are cut into long narrow lots, almost all of them vacant. The few buildings drawn are a handful of dwellings and outbuildings on the blocks between Bay and Beach avenues near Stratford, Pelham and Liberty avenues, two small buildings on the Atlantic Avenue side near Jefferis Avenue, a block 173 dwelling at the right edge and a boat house near the top right beside Liberty Thorougfare, the bay inlet. Along the ocean front a boardwalk lettered along its length runs with yellow piers, and the beach and Atlantic Ocean fill the bottom edge. The sheet carries the scale note, a compass rose and the Beach Haven date stamp of December 1922.
notes: West Avenue and Bay Avenue are now South West Avenue and South Bay Avenue; Jefferis Avenue is now Jeffries Avenue; Beach Avenue and Atlantic Avenue survive only in part south of Bay Avenue.

Only the junctions along West, Bay and Beach avenues were used as control; modern Beach Avenue and Atlantic Avenue do not reach most of the cross streets, and Nelson Avenue is cut by the left edge of the sheet and was not used.
Spelling "Thorougfare" is as lettered on the sheet.
100 ft. South end: Iroquois to Nelson Av, West Av to the ocean (Liberty, Pelham, Stratford, Jefferis, Kentford, Leeward, Merivale, Nelson).

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers the lower middle of the Beach Haven peninsula at 100 feet to an inch, from Little Egg Harbor Bay at the top to the Atlantic Ocean at the foot, and from Iroquois Avenue at the left edge to Norwood Avenue at the right edge, with north toward the upper right. The bay shore runs across the top with Liberty Thoroughfare and Mordecai Island lettered in the water, and a small wharf and boat house are drawn on the bay side near the right. Holyoak Avenue appears twice: it runs diagonally down from the bay at the upper left, and resumes lower down the page offset to the right. West Avenue, Bay Avenue, Beach Avenue and Atlantic Avenue cross the sheet from side to side, with six numbered cross streets between Holyoak Avenue and Belvoir Avenue. The ground is a plat of numbered blocks (38 to 45 along the bay, 74 to 81, 115 to 122, 153 to 160 and 191 to 198 below) cut into long narrow lots. Almost every lot is vacant; the scattered buildings are small frame dwellings and outbuildings, and they cluster near the right edge between Bay and Atlantic avenues, with one coloured as a different construction type. Four, six and eight-inch water pipes run in the streets and fire hydrants are marked on the corners. A boardwalk with piers runs along the shore at the foot of the sheet. The sheet carries the scale note, a compass rose and the Beach Haven date stamp of December 1922.
notes: West Avenue, Bay Avenue, Beach Avenue and Atlantic Avenue are now South West Avenue, South Bay Avenue, South Beach Avenue and South Atlantic Avenue; Holyoak Avenue is now Holyoke Avenue, and its drawn offset matches the two Holyoke and South West Avenue nodes about 50 m apart in OpenStreetMap.
Glendola, Fairview, Essex, Dolphin, Chatsworth and Belvoir are Glendola Avenue, Fairview Avenue, Essex Avenue, Dolphin Avenue, Chatsworth Avenue and Belvoir Avenue today.
Modern Atlantic Avenue reaches only the eastern cross streets, so only the Dolphin, Chatsworth and Belvoir junctions with it were used.
100 ft. Norwood to Iroquois Av, bay to ocean (Holyoak, Glendola, Fairview, Essex, Dolphin, Chatsworth, Belvoir).

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the north end of Beach Haven from Little Egg Harbor Bay to the Atlantic Ocean, between 5th Street on the left and 11th Street on the right, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. Along the bay side runs the Long Beach Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) with Railroad Avenue beside it; the shore of the bay, with a small inlet and a channel, is drawn above the tracks. The blocks between Railroad Avenue and Bay Avenue are shallow. Bay Avenue, Beach Avenue, Atlantic Avenue and Seaside Avenue run across the sheet, and the cross streets are 5th to 11th streets with Taylor Avenue, drawn 100 feet wide, between 8th and 9th streets. Almost all the blocks are laid out in numbered lots and are largely empty: dwellings are concentrated near 5th and 6th streets on the left and at the right edge, and the Beach Haven school house stands on Beach Avenue between 7th and 8th streets. Seaside Avenue runs along the beach below the last row of blocks. The bay, the ocean, the compass rose and the scale bars fill the margins.
notes: Bay Avenue and Atlantic Avenue are now North Bay Avenue and North Atlantic Avenue; Seaside Avenue and Railroad Avenue are not in OpenStreetMap today.
The Long Beach Railroad (P.R.R.) is gone; North Delaware Avenue appears to follow part of its line.
Beach Haven school house on Beach Avenue.
100 ft. North end: 5th to 12th St, bay to ocean, Railroad Av, Taylor Av, Seaside Av.
